subject: Quick follow-up: infra mode qualification & migration options for BrightMind
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightmind.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Novak <claire@brightmind.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / BrightMind inference needs

Thanks for the intro call this morning, Ben. Quick recap from our side and a few details you asked for on the tech landscape: 

- Current infra: a mix of an in-house API wrapping open models (custom routing) and a legacy on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA v100 nodes) used for heavy-batch batch jobs. We also experiment with a hosted LLM API for edge cases (separate vendor).
- Primary concerns: latency for real-time features, multitenant data isolation, and predictable monthly cost.
- Traffic profile: spikes at product launch windows; typical qps for inference is low-to-medium but bursty.

Wanted your take on which Redwood offering would be best: Hosted API (fast to start), Dedicated capacity (predictable), or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Also, what does migration look like from our current self-hosted cluster and the 3rd-party API?

I cc'd Claire (engineering manager) — she can provide logs/metrics if needed.

Thanks,
Amit
CTO, BrightMind AI

On Mon, Mar 28, 2026 at 09:45 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great to meet you both earlier — appreciate the clear rundown. I promised a short written follow-up with next steps and the qualification items we discussed.
>
> High-level recommendation (based on today's discovery):
>  - If you want the fastest time-to-value with minimal ops lift: start with Redwood Hosted API for a pilot of your real-time features.
>  - If you need predictable throughput and cost for production traffic with committed capacity: Redwood Dedicated is likely the best fit.
>  - If you require network isolation, audit controls, or must keep data on-prem: Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package) is the route — we can do that but it requires a slightly longer procurement and runbook alignment.
>
> For migration from on-prem GPU clusters we typically do: inventory -> compatibility scan -> model packaging/quantization -> staged rollout (canary on Dedicated or Private) -> KV/prefix cache warm-up -> cutover. From other hosted APIs, we usually build an adapter layer during the pilot so your product logic can switch endpoints with minimal changes.
>
> Action items (proposed):
> 1) Customer: share anonymized request latency histogram and peak qps (Claire).
> 2) Ben/RSE: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Claire + infra (Dylan to join).
> 3) Redwood: provide a migration checklist + rough committed-capacity sizing and ballpark pricing for Dedicated. (See attached checklist.)
>
> I attached a short checklist and a one-pager for Dedicated capacity. Happy to iterate after the tech call.
>
> Cheers,
> Ben
> Account Exec | Redwood Inference
> [Attachment: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf (12KB, PDF)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightmind.ai>, Claire Novak <claire@brightmind.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: infra mode qualification & migration options for BrightMind

Amit / Claire — quick clarifying notes before we lock a tech session: 

1) On latency: you mentioned real-time features — can you confirm SLO targets (p50/p95) and whether tail latency matters more than average? That changes the Dedicated sizing.
2) On isolation: is tenant-level encryption + separate model hosting required, or is VPC + KMS sufficient?
3) On migration complexity: do you have any custom ops in your model serving stack (custom CUDA kernels, proprietary KV cache) that would make a lift-and-shift hard?

I'll propose two time slots for a technical deep-dive and invite Dylan (solutions engineer) and Laura (sales engineering lead) to join for Dedicated/Private sizing.

Proposed tech-call slots: 
- Tue Mar 30, 11:00-12:00 PDT
- Wed Mar 31, 09:00-10:00 PDT

If you prefer, we can run a short compatibility scan first — Dylan can run a lightweight telemetry and model artifact check to estimate packaging effort (should be ~2-3 days).

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Ben Carter
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Claire Novak <claire@brightmind.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightmind.ai>
Date: 2026-03-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: infra mode qualification & migration options for BrightMind

Thanks, Ben. Quick answers: 
- SLO: p50 ~ 40-60ms, p95 ~ 180-250ms. Tail matters — user experience drops sharply above ~200ms.
- Isolation: VPC + KMS is fine for now; full on-prem not required unless legal asks change.
- Custom ops: we have a small set of CUDA kernels (image-preprocessing) and a custom caching layer for session state. We think the caching layer can be adapted.

Either Tue Mar 30 11:00 PDT works for us. We can prepare metrics export (latency histograms + a 48-hr qps sample).

Claire
Engineering Manager, BrightMind AI
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightmind.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Claire Novak <claire@brightmind.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: infra mode qualification & migration options for BrightMind

Ben / Dylan — good plan. We'll take the Tue slot. Initial preference after today's discussion: pilot on Dedicated capacity for predictable latency, then evaluate whether a Private VPC is needed later. Please include a ballpark monthly committed cost for the sizing you expect based on p95 target and burst profile.

Also, Claire will upload the latency histograms and a short export of qps to the Drive link you shared. Looking forward to the tech deep-dive.

Regards,
Amit
CTO, BrightMind AI
